html:
A written constitution adopted on 3 May 1791 by the parliament of Poland and Lithuania. It was the first modern written constitution in Europe and the second in the world, after the United States Constitution.

The Commonwealth was weak. Its great nobles could block any law with the liberum veto, a single "no" in the parliament, and neighbours bribed them to keep it that way. Russia, Prussia and Austria had already taken large slices of its land in 1772. The Great Sejm, which met from 1788, and King Stanisław August Poniatowski wanted to make the state work again.

The constitution abolished the veto and the elected kingship, split power between law makers, government and courts, and gave townspeople some rights. It offered the peasants only the protection of the law.

It lasted barely a year. Catherine the Great sent an army in 1792, backed by Polish magnates of the Targowica Confederation. The second and third partitions followed, and by 1795 the state was gone. The day, 3 May, is a national holiday in Poland.
sum: A written constitution adopted on 3 May 1791 by the parliament of Poland and Lithuania. It was the first modern written constitution in Europe and the second in the world, after the United States Constitution.
